title: SIFMA-recommended 3:00 p.m. JST early close for the Tokyo session of the USD bond market — a UK Boxing Day substitute, while JGBs and JPX run normal hours
source: NEWS: sifma.org/resources/guides-playbooks/holiday-schedule ('Holiday Schedule'), re-fetched direct 2026-09-05 (HTTP 200, 298,926 bytes) and parsed TWICE by the initial-research session: card-by-card off the rendered DOM (h3 name / date / note, region attribution fixed to the page's own 'U.S. / U.K. / Japan Holiday Recommendations' <h2> headings — 13 US, 18 UK, 35 Japan cards for 2026), and independently out of the page's embedded Next.js flight payload, where the 2027 panels a DOM parse never reaches also live (121 cards across all six panels). The Japan 2026 panel's 33rd card parses exactly as ['Boxing Day', 'Early Close Only (3:00 p.m. Japan Standard Time): Monday, December 28, 2026'] — i.e. SIFMA recommends its members' Tokyo desks close at 15:00 JST on 2026-12-28. Region attribution is self-evidencing: the note names Japan Standard Time where every US card says Eastern Time. The causing holiday is independently statutory — gov.uk/bank-holidays.json (HTTP 200, 22,207 bytes, England-and-Wales division) lists '2026-12-28 | Boxing Day | Substitute day', 2026-12-26 falling on a Saturday. Filed estimate on three counts: the confirmed-prefix taxonomy in market-events-data.ts has no slot for a trade association's recommended schedule, this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep, and the source is NON-BINDING BY ITS OWN TERMS — a recommendation to members, not exchange hours. Precedent for the class: the calendar carries sifma-bond-early-close-2026-12-31, -2027-03-25 and -2027-05-28 from the same page's US panel, plus sifma-uk-bond-market-closure-2026-12-28 and sifma-japan-early-close-2027-03-29 proposed alongside this assessment.
notes: ASSESSED 2026-09-05 — docs/research/events/sifma-japan-early-close-2026-12-28.md. THE SCOPE, and it corrects this entry's original filing: SIFMA's page states verbatim that 'All SIFMA holiday recommendations apply to the trading of U.S. dollar-denominated government securities, mortgage- and asset-backed securities, over-the-counter investment-grade and high-yield corporate bonds, municipal bonds and secondary money market trading in bankers' acceptances, commercial paper and Yankee and Euro certificates of deposit.' The three regional panels are therefore three TIME ZONES of one US-dollar market, not three asset classes — this is the Tokyo session of the USD bond market closing early, and JGBs are OUT OF SCOPE. The panel's own composition corroborates it: of its 35 cards, 19 are Japanese market holidays, 9 are US holidays and 6 are UK holidays. NOTHING JAPANESE IS SHORTENED: JPX's trading-hours page (fetched 2026-09-05, HTTP 200, 44,985 bytes) puts OSE JGB futures at 08:45-11:00 and 12:30-15:00 with a 15:02 closing auction and a NIGHT SESSION 15:30-05:55, and JPX's calendar lists no December 2026 market holiday but 12-31 — so 15:00 JST is where the listed day session ALREADY ends, and the market then trades another 14.5 hours. This retires the original filing's claim that the 08:50 JST BoJ Summary of Opinions (boj-summary-of-opinions-2026-12-28) gets 'roughly a half session for the reaction': the reaction venue is not shortened by a minute. THE NAME MISMATCH IS A RULE, NOT AN ERROR — 5 of 5 across both published years: every 'Early Close Only (3:00 p.m. Japan Standard Time)' card is a UK-ONLY bank holiday (2026-04-06 Easter Monday, 2026-08-31 Summer Bank Holiday, this one, 2027-03-29, 2027-08-30), while the two UK-only 2026 holidays with no Japan card (05-04 May Day, 05-25 Spring Bank Holiday) are exactly the two on which Tokyo is already fully closed. A US holiday shuts Tokyo's dollar desk in full; a UK-only one halves it, and SIFMA names the Tokyo card after the foreign holiday that causes it. THE THREE-REGION STATE on 2026-12-28 is the exact inverse of the triple three days later: here UK fully shut (sifma-uk-bond-market-closure-2026-12-28, proposed alongside) / Japan early close 15:00 JST / US normal session; on 12-31, US early close / Japan fully shut / UK normal. NO JAPANESE BASIS EXISTS: the Cabinet Office's statutory syukujitsu.csv (HTTP 200, 21,538 bytes) lists 18 national holidays for 2026 and ZERO in December, and 2026-12-28 is an ordinary full JPX session. IMPACT LOW, MEASURED: across 244 Tokyo sessions since 1990 with London shut (detector validated 51/52 precision, 51/51 recall against gov.uk for 2019+), the Nikkei's mean |close-to-close| runs 0.964% against 1.008% ordinary — Welch t = -0.78 — and 0.997% at t = -0.16 on the exact London-shut/New-York-open shape this date produces. An apparent 58.2% up-rate is a Monday artifact (148 of the 244 are Mondays; matched, p = 0.105). No house playbook is calendar-, holiday- or rates-keyed. HONEST LIMITS: those measurements use Japanese EQUITIES as a proxy for a dollar-bond question, since no JGB cash tape, BOJ-NET schedule or Tokyo USD-volume series was reachable; SIFMA states no normal Tokyo closing time anywhere, so the shortening's magnitude is unquantified; and SIFMA's own 2027 Japan panel gives this same holiday a 'None' recommendation, which is registered as a live falsifier (FT-sifma-japan-early-close-2026-12-28-3) rather than treated as settled.
